title: React Learning Roadmap
learning_outcomes: Explain how React Learning Roadmap relates to Introduction to React.

content_blocks.run_instructions: This is an inspectable teaching example, not an arbitrary-code runner inside CodeLeaf. Place JSX in a React/Vite project (or the relevant CSS/HTML/config file), run the project with its documented toolchain, and compare the visible behavior with the expected result. content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Use the code as a small experiment for React Learning Roadmap. First predict the result, then run or inspect it in the required runtime. Change one input and explain why the output changed. If the topic depends on React version or framework support, confirm that the project uses a compatible version before interpreting a result.

content_blocks.title: Version and environment note
content_blocks.text: This course assumes the React 19.3 documentation snapshot dated 2026-10-12. Core component, JSX, props, state, and event concepts apply broadly; modern APIs and server rendering must be checked against the stated React version and the framework/runtime in use.

content.task: Create a minimal example demonstrating React Learning Roadmap. Include the relevant subtopic “Required JavaScript concepts”, explain the expected UI/result, and verify one normal case plus one boundary or failure case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates the named concept rather than merely mentioning it.
The expected visible or logged result is documented and reproducible.
At least one boundary, empty, loading, or failure case is handled or explained.
The implementation remains accessible and does not introduce avoidable mutation, stale state, or insecure client-only trust.
hints: Start with the smallest part of “Required JavaScript concepts” that can be observed independently.
Write down what should appear before changing the code; then change one input at a time.
Use the browser console, React Developer Tools, or the appropriate test/runtime to isolate a mismatch.
content.expected_output: The ref points at the input after commit; optional chaining protects the not-yet-mounted case.

common_mistakes.problem: The example handles only the happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Real UI receives empty values, delayed responses, and invalid input.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one explicit edge/failure case and document the expected message or state.

common_mistakes.problem: The example stores redundant data or mutates an existing array/object.
common_mistakes.why: The displayed result can drift from the source data or React may not observe the intended change.
common_mistakes.fix: Derive values where possible and create a new value when updating state.

common_mistakes.problem: A browser or framework capability is assumed to exist everywhere.
common_mistakes.why: Availability can depend on the host runtime, React version, and framework.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the official reference, declare the runtime/version, and provide a fallback when appropriate.
